translationRepairs: Tian Rong said, "Chu must kill Tian Jia and Zhao must kill Jiao and Xian—only then will I send troops."
Tian Rong said, "Chu must kill Tian Jia and Zhao must kill Jiao and Jian—only then will I send troops."
Focus unit 趙殺角、閒 names 閒; adjacent s0052 has 田閒 rendered Tian Jian, so idiomatic 'Xian' is a wrong reading of the same personal name.
Tian Rong said, "Only if Chu kills Tian Jia and Zhao kills Jiao and Xian will I send out troops."
Tian Rong said, "Only if Chu kills Tian Jia and Zhao kills Jiao and Jian will I send out troops."
The same 閒 in 趙殺角、閒 is Tian Jian, matching s0052's 田閒; literal 'Xian' is the same mistranslation.
Tian Jia, Tian Jiao, and Tian Xian are in Chu and Zhao. They are not close kin like hands and feet—why will they not kill them?
Tian Jia, Tian Jiao, and Tian Jian are in Chu and Zhao. They are not close kin like hands and feet—why will they not kill them?
Focus unit lists 田假、田角、田閒; 田閒 is Tian Jian, not Tian Xian, as confirmed by the same name in s0052.
Tian Jia, Tian Jiao, and Tian Xian are in Chu and Zhao; they are not kin like hands and feet to those rulers—why do they not kill them?
Tian Jia, Tian Jiao, and Tian Jian are in Chu and Zhao; they are not kin like hands and feet to those rulers—why do they not kill them?
Literal 'Tian Xian' likewise misreads 田閒; the proposed Tian Jian matches the Chinese personal name and chapter usage.
Tian Heng feared he would be put to death, so he and more than five hundred followers went to sea and settled in the Minzhong islands.
Tian Heng feared he would be put to death, so he and more than five hundred followers put to sea and settled on an island.
The local 闯 is an OCR corruption of 島, confirmed by the Shiji parallel. The revision removes the invented Minzhong toponym and renders the singular island naturally.
Tian Heng feared execution, so he and more than five hundred followers put to sea and lived in the Minzhong islands.
Tian Heng feared execution, so he and more than five hundred followers put to sea and lived on an island.
The parallel has 居島中. The literal revision removes the invented place-name and states that Tian Heng's party lived on an island.

Tian Heng declined, saying, "I boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji. Now I hear his younger brother Shang is a valued Han general. I am afraid and dare not obey; I ask only to remain a commoner and keep to the Minzhong islands."

Tian Heng declined, saying, "I boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji. Now I hear his younger brother Shang is a valued Han general. I am afraid and dare not obey; I ask only to remain a commoner and stay on an island at sea."
The Shiji parallel has 守海島中. Here 守 means to remain, not to guard, and the revision removes the invented Minzhong place-name.

Tian Heng declined, saying, "Your servant boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji. Now I hear that his younger brother Shang is a Han general and a man of talent. I am afraid and dare not obey the summons; I ask only to remain a commoner and guard the Minzhong islands."

Tian Heng declined, saying, "Your servant boiled Your Majesty's envoy Li Yiji. Now I hear that his younger brother Shang is a Han general and a man of talent. I am afraid and dare not obey the summons; I ask only to remain a commoner and stay on an island at sea."
The parallel 守海島中 means remaining on an island at sea, not guarding a group of islands. The revision removes the unsupported Minzhong name.

Together with his generals Manqiu Chen of Baitu and Wang Huang, he established Zhao Li, a descendant of the Zhao line, as king, gathered Xin's scattered soldiers again, and plotted with Xin and Modun to attack Han.

Together with his generals Manqiu Chen of Baitu and Wang Huang, he established Zhao Li, a descendant of the Zhao line, as king, gathered Xin's scattered soldiers again, and plotted with Xin and Modu to attack Han.
Focus unit 冒頓 is Modu; the same unit's literal and other chapter units already use Modu, so idiomatic 'Modun' is an inconsistent misspelling.

In the early Taichu period, he served as raiding general stationed at the outer bastions of Wuyuan, then returned as Director of Splendid Happiness, investigated witchcraft in the crown prince's palace, and was killed by the crown prince.

During the Taichu period, he served as raiding general stationed at the outer bastions of Wuyuan, then returned as Director of Splendid Happiness, investigated witchcraft in the crown prince's palace, and was killed by the crown prince.
太初中 means during the Taichu era, not specifically its early part; dropping 'early' corrects an unwarranted temporal narrowing.

Zeng began young as a palace attendant, rose through the various offices to attendant-in-ordinary and director of splendid happiness, and under Emperor Zhao reached front general; together with Grand General Huo Guang he settled the succession and enthroned Emperor Xuan, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.

Zeng entered palace service as a young man and served in the various bureaus, as Palace Attendant, and as Grandee of Splendid Light. Under Emperor Zhao he rose to Front General. Together with Grand General Huo Guang, he settled the succession and enthroned Emperor Xuan, for which his fief was increased by one thousand households.
光祿大夫 is Grandee of Splendid Light, while 侍中 is Palace Attendant. The revision separates the offices and renders 定策立宣帝 as settling the succession and enthroning Emperor Xuan.
